_comment: Treatment-group classification rules. Stage 1 (patterns): the first matching entry in 'patterns' (substring on UPPER-cased filename) decides the base treatment. Stage 2 (modifiers): every entry in 'modifiers' is then scanned over the *whole* filename and, when present, appended as ' + <label>' to the base — this lets NORBAEO_HARMIN be classified as 'Norbaeocystin + harmine' without enumerating every BASE+MODIFIER combination. Stage 3 (concentrations / time_points / washouts): each list is a sequence of [regex, label] rules; the first regex in each list whose .search() hits the UPPER-cased filename contributes ONE qualifier, appended to the label with ' | <qualifier>'. Final order: base[+ modifiers][ | concentration][ | time_point][ | washout]. Loaded via synaptic_ssl.clustering.groups.load_group_patterns / load_group_modifiers / load_concentration_patterns / load_time_patterns / load_washout_patterns.
_ordering: Order of 'patterns' is significant — place more specific patterns before more general ones (NORPSI before PSI, NORBAEO/NORBAO before BAEO). Order within each regex list (concentrations / time_points / washouts) is also first-match-wins, so place more specific regexes first.
_typo_aliases: Filename typos observed in the data are mapped to their canonical group: NORBAO (missing E in NORBAEO) and HRMIN (missing A in HARMIN). Keep them adjacent to the canonical entries so audit diffs stay readable.
_modifier_self_match: A modifier pattern that is identical to the base pattern that matched (e.g. base HARMIN matched a HARMIN-only filename) is *not* re-appended, so HARMIN-only files stay 'Harmine' rather than 'Harmine + harmine'.
_qualifier_regex_notes: Regexes run against UPPER-cased filename. Concentration: (?<![0-9]) prevents '1UM' matching inside '01UM'/'10UM'; (?![A-Z0-9]) prevents matching inside longer tokens. Time: (?<![0-9]) prevents matching inside dates (e.g. '20251024HOD' would be excluded if it existed); [_ ]? allows both '24HOD' and '24_HOD'; (?=[^A-Z]|$) requires the char after HOD to be non-letter (or end). Washout: '1H10UM' (1-hour pulse with 10 uM) followed by optional separator then 'WO' → flag '1h pulse' (the concentration regex independently picks '10 uM' and the time regex independently picks the time after WO).
